title: Collection namespace normalization redirects staging retention into the live hotel catalog
fault_primitive: ConfigMap-deployed maintenance controller truncates a dotted MongoDB collection name, repeatedly reapplying TTL cleanup and cache invalidation
incident_class: A controller qualified-name parser drops a MongoDB collection namespace and applies staging retention to live data
symptoms: Hotel search and some recommendations close HTTP connections with recovered nil-address panics. Profile RPCs can succeed with empty profiles. Most catalog documents, all services, and all application pods remain healthy. Frontend runtime-error logs surge.
why_hard: Recovered frontend serialization panics occur several hops from a successful profile RPC. Only five of eighty live documents vanish, so ordinary counts and hotel-1 checks pass. The policy correctly names staging.hotels, hiding the root cause from a config-only review; a SQL-style qualified-name parser actually chooses hotels. MongoDB misses become immortal empty memcached profiles. The companion recreates indexes, deletes republished records, and invalidates cache keys, so restarts, index removal, data restoration, and cache flushing alone fail.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Treat frontend panics as a frontend release issue because upstream RPCs finish successfully
Inspect hotel 1 or catalog counts and conclude profile storage is healthy
Restart the profile service to regenerate its sample catalog without correcting retention scope
Drop the TTL index without stopping the periodic reconciliation that recreates it
Restore missing documents but overlook immortal empty profile entries in memcached
Flush memcached without correcting the controller and restoring missing records
Accept the correct-looking staging.hotels policy without checking how the companion resolves MongoDB collection names
mitigation_summary: Repair the mounted controller to preserve the full MongoDB collection name, reload it, remove the live TTL index, restore revisions from hotel_catalog_versions, and flush memcached-profile. All required information is in the cluster.
